parties:
Nemai Kumar ------ Appellant
Vs.
Ramesh Chandra Dutta & Others ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 9. The Court of appeal below did not properly place the onus of proof on the parties to prove their cases. The Court of appeal below proceeded on the basis that there were two brothers of a Hindu Dayabhaga School, and in the name of Rajani the property was acquired. It was for the other brother Nishi Kanta to show that there was a joint family and there was joint fund, and the property was acquired cut of joint fund. Proceeding from that basis the lower Appellate Court found that the defendant failed to prove his case. On this finding the suit was decreed. The learned Judge of the High Court proceeded on the basis that the appeal was concluded by finding of fact, without examining whether there was proper allocation of onus of proof by the Court of appeal below. The Court of appeal below as well as the High Court found that the two brothers Rajani and Nishi separated themselves only 7/8 years before the death of Rajani which was in 1959. They also found that the brothers were in joint family. The Court of appeal below also found that Rajani and Nishi shifted to the present premises in 1924 (1331 B.S.) It has also been found that both the brothers sold their ancestral property in 1943. We find that both the learned Single Judge as well as the Court of appeal below were in error in placing the onus. The finding of the Court of appeal below was enough to establish a joint Hindu family with joint property, and therefore the initial onus on the defendent was discharged, and so the presumption drawn by the trial Court that the property acquired by Rajani in his name is to be presumed to have been acquired by or for the joint family cannot be said to be erroneous, since the contrary has not been shown by the plaintiff. The onus having shifted on to the plaintiff to show the contrary it is now to be seen whether the plaintiff, who is the son of Rajani, by evidence has proved satisfactorily, that nonetheless the family was joint and the property was acquired in the state of jointers, still the property was purchased by Rajani not only by his own name and out of his own fund, but was kept outside the joint property. There is no credible evidence or any finding to this effect, whereas the trial Court on a consideration of evidence held that the presumption has not been dislodged and we do not find any error in the findings of the trial Court. The Court of appeal below as well as learned Judge of the High Court both committed an error in law in allocating the onus of proof in the case.
